summary: Lists the name, commands, and libraries for the Capital Projects web app.
purpose: Tells the package manager what to install and gives the commands to run, build, preview, and check the app.
why: Likely reason: a Vite and React app needs many interface and tooling libraries, and this file lists them.
how: 1. Name the package as a private workspace piece. 2. Define four commands: dev, build, serve, and typecheck. 3. List most interface and tooling libraries as development dependencies. 4. List the runtime libraries, which are the file-upload kit and the mermaid diagram library.
inputs: Installed through the workspace package manager. Several versions come from a shared catalog outside this file.
outputs: Four commands: start a development server, build the app, preview the build, and check types.
risks: The dev and serve commands listen on all network addresses, so anyone who can reach the machine can open the app. Most libraries are development dependencies, so a production-only install could break the build.
debug: If install fails, check that the shared catalog entries exist. If the dev server cannot be reached, check its host and port. If the build fails, run typecheck first to see the type errors.
